feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong strategic + technical positioning: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels senior and marketable.  
- Generally clean, professional writing with concrete scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include results like traffic growth, email engagement, production savings, campaign performance, or operational efficiencies to strengthen impact.  
- Reduce duplication and tighten structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating them would improve scannability.  
- Fix minor style/consistency issues: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; add the serial comma consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement”); standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current seniority and scope: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years…”
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with sharper, evidence-aligned wording such as “leading” or “specializing in.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel communications, CMS modernization, and building the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex teams. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Platform modernization” overlaps with Topline Skills/Technical sections; consider specifying “CMS modernization” for clarity.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too close to the summary and Topline Skills, so it reads as a third version of the same message. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-level strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Cross-functional stakeholder coordination,” “Web platform and CMS administration.”
- Replace generic items with more senior, distinctive ones: “Digital governance,” “Content operations,” or “Platform modernization” instead of “Workflow & systems architecture.”
- Reorder by strategic value and recency: Digital strategy & transformation • Content operations & editorial workflows • Web platform/CMS administration • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Consider trimming to 6–7 items for sharper focus and easier scanning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- Web, analytics, multimedia, and workflow themes are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + value: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets, e.g.:
- “Designed and improved digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to support coordinated cross-channel communications.”
- “Built Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Provided hands-on CMS/front-end implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user discovery experience.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “Drupal/web improvement” strongly overlap with the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consultant capacity, new initiatives, and AI/search work.
- The microsite/campaign examples also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Make bullets more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: quantify team size, budget, newsletter/social growth, video output, cost savings, reporting adoption, or efficiency gains from governance changes.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “including”/“along with” constructions with direct verbs; combine analytics tools into one concise bullet focused on decision-making impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this at a higher strategic/organizational level.
- Video studio/building recurring multimedia content overlaps with older NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize first-institutionalized capability or operational scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like broad responsibility than distinct impact. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: managed 4 weekly newsletters; launched/scaled weekly advocacy video update; coordinated editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Replace soft phrasing like “helped scale,” “helped improve,” and “strengthened” with stronger verbs: “streamlined,” “standardized,” “expanded,” “institutionalized.”
- Add metrics if available: email open/click rates, video views, production volume, publishing turnaround, stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video” and “weekly video updates” also appear in the prior role and footer project list; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the channel.
- “Publishing workflows” and cross-team coordination overlap with Director of Digital Media; keep this entry focused on executional leadership before enterprise oversight.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, differentiated language tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Enterprise web governance and content operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent consulting/director work.
- Keep wording parallel: use noun phrases, avoid mixing leadership traits with execution terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; make this section more distinctive or more senior.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to enterprise web modernization rather than exhaustive tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization” instead of listing multiple CMSs equally.
- Prioritize recent/high-impact strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search; de-emphasize older/basic items like jQuery.
- Tighten wording and group related items: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)” and “Workflow automation and Airtable-based systems.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation and Airtable-based systems • SharePoint and Power Pages • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool lists to the technical section.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. This topline item should emphasize higher-level capability and decision impact rather than repeat platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to strategic outcomes: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating platforms: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten phrasing to show application, e.g.: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO and digital performance optimization”
- If space allows, use one stronger term: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding” or “Decision-ready reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- Since recent NACo experience already names these tools, avoid repeating the full stack here unless you elevate it to strategy/impact language.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo multimedia bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability tied to recent leadership and studio buildout.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, outcome-oriented phrasing:

- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio operations and production workflows

- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing formats like broad functions (“livestreaming”) with equipment (“PTZ camera systems”) unless all bullets are capability-based.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” and “livestream operations” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” partially overlaps with recent NACo studio/event bullets, so this skills item should stay broad, not narrative.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth/recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, order by strongest/recentest platform: put Drupal first and consider grouping lower-use tools last.
- Add version/scope only where credible and recent, e.g., “Drupal 10” instead of just “Drupal,” since that aligns with recent project work.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages…”). Keep one list broad and make the other more outcome-/scope-specific.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus the enterprise focus of the CV unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical breadth, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions • **Tagging & tracking:** Google Tag Manager
- Drop version numbers unless they matter; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- Consider replacing broad terms with stronger specifics if accurate, e.g., “REST API integrations,” “serverless scripting,” or “CI/CD automation.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to outcomes in recent roles rather than here, e.g., implementations supporting Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, or workflow automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” to reduce fragmentation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split into two tighter categories to show intent: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and “Work management & collaboration: Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.”
- Cut lower-value/older/general tools unless they are current and used recently; Basecamp and Trello are the easiest to remove.
- If space allows, add a short qualifier instead of a pure list, e.g. “Built workflow automation and cross-team planning systems using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack and Teams.”
- Order by relevance to recent roles and impact, with automation tools first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar project-management signals; listing all four adds little differentiation.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a basic tool list and misses the scale or type of email/engagement work you led. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show application, e.g. **newsletter, campaign automation, and member communications platforms**
- Keep the strongest/most recent enterprise tool first; if Dynamics 365 was only limited exposure, move **Higher Logic** first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter scale or email leadership here; that impact is already covered well in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 experience entries.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications claims elsewhere, so keep this item strictly tool-based.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results if known: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams/videos produced, newsletter volume, audience growth, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specifics such as “supported website refresh,” “produced weekly video updates,” and “coordinated livestream delivery.”
- Consider ending with light supervisory scope: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as launching or piloting the format, not leading/expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” is repeated elsewhere; keep this version focused on team formation and hands-on production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If you can, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded member engagement.
- Consider a two-bullet format for readability and to separate program/research work from media execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is too broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later digital roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia work here; later entries already establish video/content leadership more credibly.
